rows.reason: Fixes rounds 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 hold. Five sentences of 13, 11, 13, 15 and 15 words, each ending on a full stop, with no first person. Every citation checks: the cardigan of a girl who 'had left' is across lines 13 and 14; 'the Friday box' is on line 33; 'It won't fit me next year.' is on line 47 word for word; 'September football trials' is on line 38. The contrast word 'Yet' is kept (round 5). 'On next year' and the September link are restored (round 6). Nothing argues from silence (round 2), and the key comes only in the last sentence. But sentence 4 brings back the round-3 fault: 'But Miss Bhatt's long look on line 48 shows he is giving up on next year.' Line 48 says she looked 'a second or two longer than the answer needed'. The words that make this evidence are 'than the answer needed', because they say his size reason did not satisfy her. The paraphrase 'long look' drops exactly those words. A long look alone shows nothing about next year. The sentence also makes the look the thing that 'shows' the conclusion. At most, the look shows the size reason is not the whole story. 'Giving up on next year' only follows when the look is combined with the cardigan/jumper contrast and his own 'next year' on line 47. So a child sent to line 48 is told it proves something it cannot prove alone. Round 3 was refused because this step was 'asserted, not shown'. Rounds 4 to 6 fixed it with the quotation and the middle step ('looks "longer than the answer needed", so size is not everything'), and round 6 said to keep that sentence. This draft removes both. On an inference question an inference step is fair, but this one has to be drawn from quoted evidence. Here it is pinned on a paraphrase that removes the evidence. Fix: keep sentences 1 to 3. Restore sentence 4 as round 6 had it: 'On line 48 Miss Bhatt looks "longer than the answer needed", so size is not everything.' Then carry the conclusion into the last sentence, e.g. 'Giving up on next year, he won't fill the "September football trials" sheet on line 38.' (15 words). Minor: 'its space' never names the room at the bottom (line 39), which is acceptable since the stem quotes it. The key is still the one defensible answer; the fault is in the script, not the question.
